summary.intent: Plan (research → design pass → plan → verify) and then execute GSD phase 69 — a large Rust port adding FUSE/WinFsp integration with grant-root awareness (TEST-03, SC#1–#6, decisions D-01–D-08) to the CipherBox codebase — running unattended overnight via --auto.
summary.outcome: All 14 plans (waves 1–7) were written, verified by gsd-plan-checker with no blockers, coverage-gated (TEST-03 + 8/8 decisions), and committed (23b4ba198); execution then began, with the Wave 1 canary plan 69-01 (Node enum/codec) successfully validated end-to-end through executor→worktree→merge→cargo-check before fanning out the rest of Wave 1.

repo: The grant-root scope-computation algorithm has a complete TS reference at packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/scope.ts, making the Rust port a port-not-design-from-scratch task.
activeGrantRootIpnsNames comes from GET /shares/sent, which has no crates/api-client wrapper yet — a hidden blast-radius gap surfaced by research.
The desktop E2E CI workflow's real name is 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as ROADMAP/CONTEXT word it — gh workflow run with the wrong name would 404.

cipher-box-phase69 is itself a linked git worktree of the cipher-box repo, so execute-phase's worktree-isolated agents nest one level deeper under .claude/worktrees/ — orchestrator_root pinning in the manifest must account for this.
The API-SURFACE regen tool is TS/JS-focused; on Rust-only phases it returns symbolCount: 0/stale:true and should be treated as an empty hint rather than an error.

69-13-PLAN.md explicitly defers the Windows spawn_file_meta_reencrypt caller and the whole-tree SC#2 gate to 69-14, which plan-checker later confirmed as a consistent, intentional hand-off between the two plans.
workflow: GSD planner crashes mid-response (API connection closed) still leave completed plans on disk (§9a filesystem-fallback) — recovery should diff what's on disk vs. what the partial summary referenced rather than restarting from scratch.

When a planner crash leaves a gap, spawn a fresh gsd-planner in single-plan mode for just the missing plan rather than re-running the full multi-plan planner, preserving role separation and avoiding redoing completed work.

The commit_failed status from the GSD commit helper is a known false-negative — always verify via git log/git status before treating it as a real failure or retrying (consistent with existing memory feedback-gsd-commit-reword-verify-first).

Planners may use ad-hoc pseudo-IDs (e.g. SC-01..SC-06) in a plan's requirements: frontmatter instead of the actual phase requirement ID (TEST-03) — the §13 requirements-coverage gate depends on the real ID being present, so this must be checked/fixed explicitly.

For a large unattended --auto multi-wave execution, canary-run the first plan synchronously (not fanned out in parallel) to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before dispatching the rest of the wave in parallel.

friction: gsd-planner died mid-response with an API connection-closed error while writing plan 69-14, requiring manual disk-state diagnosis and a resume/handoff cycle (including a scheduled 40-minute wakeup).
Plans on disk used pseudo requirement IDs (SC-01..SC-06) instead of the real TEST-03 ID, which would have silently failed the §13 requirements-coverage gate if not caught.
